newsitem.title: USA: Kellstrom to buy International Aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Kellstrom to buy International Aircraft.

text.p: Kellstrom Industries Inc said it has signed a definitive agreement to purchase substantially all of the assets and assume certain liabilities of San Carlos, Calif.-based International Aircraft Support LP ("IASI").

Kellstrom said it has agreed to pay about $26.5 million in cash and warrants to purchase 500,000 Kellstrom common stock at $9.25 per share. The warrants expire two years from the closing, which is expected within 90 days.
Kellstrom said it has named Alex. Brown & Sons as placement agent for the senior and subordinated debt it intends to issue to finance the cash portion of the acquisition.
Kellstrom said it expects to retain IASI's personnel and is negotiating long-term employment agreements with its senior management to be implemented upon completion of the acquisition.
Kellstrom said it expects that 31-year aviation industry executive Fred von Husen, president and chief executive of IASI since 1987, will become executive vice president of Kellstrom.
IASI, founded in 1979 and privately owned, is a leading international reseller of commercial jet engines and engine parts, Kellstrom said.

Its customers include major airlines, engine overhaul facilities including those operated by airlines, independent overhaul and maintenance organizations and aircraft engine manufacturers, Kellstrom said.

For the most part, IASI's customer base does not overlap with that of Kellstrom, and therefore the addition of IASI's distribution network will be a substantial enhancement for Kellstrom, especially in Europe.

Kellstrom said it intends to utilize the presence of IASI's management and IASI's 50,000 square foot warehouse facilities in the San Francisco area, among other things, to support and expand its activity in the Pacific Rim.

Closing of the transaction is subject to completion by Alex. Brown & Sons of the $26.5 million debt financing according to terms approved by Kellstrom's Board of Directors and satisfactory results of legal and accounting due diligence.
